title: Katie Maloney Wasn’t Interested in Reality TV After ‘Vanderpump Rules.’ Then Came Stassi Schroeder
full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 8, 2026 12:00pm Katie Maloney at the 'House of Stassi' premiere in New York. Disney/Arthur Gareev Logo text Katie Maloney wasn’t rushing back to reality television after Vanderpump Rules aired its last season with the original cast in 2024. But then, Stassi Schroeder called. Longtime friends who starred alongside one another throughout the golden years of the Emmy-nominated Bravo series, Schroeder invited Maloney to appear on her new Hulu series House of Stassi after the core cast had been assembled. It’s a topic discussed on the new series, which dropped on the streamer on July 29. During their first onscreen sit-down, a first meeting after a fallout a few years back, at the Belmont (an obvious Vanderpump Rules callback), Maloney gives it to Schroeder straight. Related Stories TV Barbarians at the Gate: How Reality Stars Crashed Hollywood's A-List TV Stassi Schroeder Knew Her Hulu Series Would Cause a Stir: "We Set Out to Make the Realest Show We Could" “You just make your world smaller and smaller and smaller to the point where it’s like if, I don’t know, they didn’t come out of you or they’re not married to you or they’re not on your fucking payroll, they don’t get to be in your life,” Maloney told her friend, cut to a scene of Schroeder, who is an executive producer, uttering, “Damn, this bitch is good. And that’s the type of truth-telling we need on reality TV . I need her to do this show.” Maloney tells The Hollywood Reporter that she wouldn’t have signed up for another reality TV show if it weren’t for “the people that are involved.” She adds, “Knowing Stassi’s history with reality TV and her perspective on it, how she wanted to navigate doing the show was something that I really aligned with.” “Especially coming off of a show like Vanderpump Rules , which was very successful for a long time, but really did kind of, at the end, take a toll on me,” Maloney says, continuing, “I just knew that if I was going to return, it would have to be for something that felt very different, and that absolutely was the case. I just really trusted the producers and the whole production team, and it just was exciting.” Katie Maloney sits down with Stassi Schroeder on House of Stassi. Disney Maloney knew the series was in the works (it was first announced in August 2024, three months before Bravo revealed it was rebooting Vanderpump Rules ), but “never considered [joining the cast] to be an option for a number of reasons.” “I didn’t know where they were in the process,” Maloney explains, adding that she quickly learned they hadn’t started shooting for House of Stassi , and things fell into place. “I don’t know. There was just something that, maybe just innately in my gut, told me like, this is the time ,” she says. A seasoned reality star, Maloney was “cautious” about joining a new show and the cycle that emerges while starring on an active series. “That’s a lot of what I’ve been enjoying away from reality TV, out of the public eye and constant attention,” she says, “but at the same time, I’m pretty used to this, so I have a pretty good handle on it.” She also admits she wasn’t eager to jump at other reality TV experiences after Vanderpump Rules ended. “Obviously, the same production team that worked on Vanderpump Rules worked on The Valley , and I, just through casual conversations, have made it clear that that was not something I’d ever be interested in. But I didn’t really have the interest for a while in participating in reality TV.” Maloney worked with Bravo for over a decade; she was one of three original cast members to remain on Vanderpump Rules for its 11-season tenure before the network rebooted the show. House of Stassi ushers her onto a new network on Hulu and Freeform, which Disney backs. “I’m trying to not compare it constantly,” Maloney says when asked about the differences in starring on a new network. “It’s hard because, like with anything, that’s sort of my only frame of reference. But I’m trying to just treat it like it’s something entirely new that I’ve never been a part of.” Maloney did bring one part of her Vanderpump past over to House of Stassi : an Ariana Madix cameo. “She without hesitation agreed to do it,” Maloney says, explaining that she told Madix she wanted to film at their West Hollywood sandwich shop Something About Her . “I was never going to press [Ariana] or ask her to be part of it beyond that, but I was just happy that she was so supportive,” she says. “Also, we worked so hard to get our sandwich shop open, so it was important that for the first time us filming there, that she was there for that.” On the new series, some House of Stassi castmembers raised their quarrels with Maloney joining their cast. She admits she did not know people like Kristina Kelly and Taylor Strecker had such strong hesitations about her being back around their friend group. “Not prior to going into it. Obviously, I found out quickly that some people had issues,” she says. One comment she was not given a heads up about before the show dropped came from Schroeder’s husband Beau Clark, who said he hoped Schroeder reconnecting with Maloney wouldn’t shift his wife’s behavior. “The only [comment] I had no idea that was said was Beau’s reaction. And obviously Stassi and I having our friendship break that we had, that’s his wife, he’s gonna have her back, but he was pretty passionate in his feelings about me,” Maloney says. “That one stung a little bit too because I’ve always loved Beau and really gotten along with him, so kind of sucked to hear.” Stassi Schroeder, Kristina Kelly and Katie Maloney celebrate the premiere of House of Stassi. Disney/Arthur Gareev A House of Stassi moment of Maloney’s that stuck out was a confessional interview before the season’s disastrous Queen Mary finale dinner party, where Schroeder and Clark’s friends and family brought up concerns about their marriage. “I know how common affairs are and how they happen, and I’ve experienced the beginning stages of it,” she said on the show, sharing her experience of emotional abandonment in her marriage and how she found connection outside of that relationship. Some viewers thought Maloney was speaking about Tom Schwartz’s infidelities in their former marriage, but Maloney confirms she “was talking about myself,” and that “not that many people have caught onto” her admission in the finale episode. “I’ve seen it happen over and over too in people’s lives that I know. If you stop and think about it, five times out of five times, when someone ends their marriage or long-term relationship, the common thing that’s said at the end is, ‘I felt like we were roommates,’” she says. “And that’s when you feel emotional abandonment, and that’s when, and I’m speaking from my perspective on things and other people’s perspectives, but I think that it’s so common.” “It wasn’t necessarily like a singular person or anything,” Maloney adds. “I just was aware so clearly of where I stood emotionally within my marriage and relationship, and some people choose to explore that well out without exiting the relationship armors, because that’s a more difficult thing to do. I recognized that that was my time.” Moving forward with a potential second season of House of Stassi , Maloney says she’d be on board: “I think that would be a lot of fun. I’d love to.” As for what to expect from her, she’d want to “repair and build some of the fractures in the relationships that I have,” while also continuing to grow her friendship with Schroeder. “[I want to] grow my relationship with Stassi from where we are now in this season of life that’s so different than the one that we met each other in,” Maloney says. “I just am excited to see where that goes and takes us.” *** Season one of House of Stassi is now streaming on Hulu. THR

title: Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” About Tonight’s Closing Of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’; Composer Hopes Broadway Will “Come To Its Senses”
full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Madonna Pays Tribute To Late ‘Ray Of Light’ Producer William Orbit: “Your Music Gave Me A Magic Carpet To Fly On” Morrissey Cancels This Month’s Four-Show Las Vegas Residency Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” About Tonight’s Closing Of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’; Composer Hopes Broadway Will “Come To Its Senses” View All August 8, 2026 10:30am André De Shields as Old Deuteronomy in Cats: The Jellicle Ball Matthew Murphy and Evan Zimmerman for MurphyMade Composer Andrew Lloyd Webber is “gutted” that the Broadway production of his Cats: The Jellicle Ball is closing tonight at the Broadhurst Theatre, five months earlier than originally planned. In an emotional message posted on Instagram, Lloyd Webber says he hopes the show’s closing will serve as a warning about “the unsustainable cost” of producing new shows on Broadway. Related Stories Reviews ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ Broadway Review: A Queer, Radiant Reinvention Makes A Lasting Memory News ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ Scores Best Week Ever As Closing Date Nears – Broadway Box Office “I’m gutted that the wonderful Broadway production of Cats: The Jellicle Ball is closing today,” he writes. “I’m immensely proud to have been a part of an incredibly daring production whose cast and creative team broke new ground on Broadway and gave 17 actors their Broadway debut.” He continues, “Maybe the show’s closing just might be remembered as the moment that caused everyone involved with Broadway to come to their senses and address the unsustainable cost of producing and running any new show now on The Great White Way, let alone saying new work.” Watch on Deadline See the message below, along with a note of thanks to fans from the show’s producers who teased “a lot more Jellicle joy to bring to this world” in the days ahead. Today’s message isn’t the first time Lloyd Webber has expressed his disappointment about the early closing. Last month, when the August 8 closing date was announced, he wrote, in part, “As someone who is still as in love with Broadway as I was when I was a teenager, I beg the theatre owners, unions and producers to come together urgently to address what is a crisis coming to a head. Broadway is in dire danger of rivalling Hollywood’s empty soundstages with increasingly dark theatres.” That IG post drew both praise and harsh criticism among commenters. While Sunset Blvd. star Nicole Scherzinger commended Lloyd Webber as “exactly the person” to “help drive the change that’s needed,” others rejected his seeming equating of landlords and union members in sharing the responsibility of Broadway’s financial uncertainties. “So have the audacity to call out out Shubert Organization which has a monopoly on almost half the Broadway theaters,” wrote one of Lloyd Webber’s followers. “Call out their greed. They want producers to cover the rent and the entire operating costs. They want to keep the telecharge fees which they own. How is this allowed?” Wrote a member of a costume crew, “Leave the union workers out of this we deserve to be paid fairly for our work. if you can’t afford to pay us fairly then you can’t afford to produce a show right. Very dangerous to include the unions in this to be honest,” while actor and dancer Neil Haskell wrote, “Most Broadway actors can barely afford to live in the city.” Tonight’s closing will almost certainly have at least one immediate impact: A bump in final-week ticket sales. While the box office report for the week won’t be out until Tuesday, last week’s figures showed Cats: The Jellicle Ball posting its best box office numbers ever as last-chancers scrambled for seats. The production was at standing room only for the week ending August 2, grossing $1,405,709. That’s an increase of $216,278 over the previous week. Regarding today’s message from the composer, at least one famous commenter and Broadway devotee had a suggestion. “Why didn’t alw just fund it himself,” commented Rosie O’Donnell. “he’s a billionaire.” A big fan of the show, O’Donnell did add a “Like” to Lloyd Webber’s message. title: Olivia Wilde Talks Fight To Get ‘The Invite’ A Theatrical Release Following Sundance Response: “I Was Passionate About It With A Lot Of Support”
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Olivia Wilde Talks Fight To Get ‘The Invite’ A Theatrical Release Following Sundance Response: “I Was Passionate About It With A Lot Of Support” Sigurjón Sighvatsson Talks Rise Of Propaganda Films & Battles To Get David Lynch’s ‘Wild At Heart’ & ‘Twin Peaks’ Off The Ground – Locarno Elisabeth Moss, Daphne Schmon & Ash Mayfair Select 12 Finalists For Wscripted 2026 Screenplay List View All August 8, 2026 9:45am Olivia Wilde Deadline Olivia Wilde has revealed that she was “passionate” about getting a theatrical release for The Invite following the audience response to the comedy at Sundance. “I wanted to investigate this phenomenon that we found at Sundance when we felt the film have that chemical reaction with the audience the first time and it was extraordinary,” she told a press conference at the Locarno Film Festival where the film screens on the Piazza Grande this evening. “I thought, well, this was magic. We have to listen to this… we have to fight for it,” she continued. “If you don’t fight for it, listen, you know this… they bribe you to not take theatrical. It’s a bribe. You get paid more. Not me, not the filmmaker. The financiers will get a lot more money to go to streaming, and you can take that bribe and give that up if that’s where your priorities lie.” Related Stories News Sigurjón Sighvatsson Talks Rise Of Propaganda Films & Battles To Get David Lynch's 'Wild At Heart' & 'Twin Peaks' Off The Ground - Locarno News Felix Randau Reveals Why Claes Bang Was Perfect For The Role Of Himmler's Shady Masseur In 'I Is Another': "If Claes Tells You A Lie, You Want To Believe Him" Wilde thanked producer Megan Ellison at Annapurna for getting on board with her desire to get the film into cinemas, and agreeing to accept A24 ‘s theatrical offer, hinting that the streamers had gone higher. She also credited FilmNation Entertainment , which co-handled the domestic sale with UTA, for securing individual theatrical distributors internationally. Watch on Deadline Olivia Wilde Talks Fight To Get 'The Invite' A Theatrical Release Following Positive Sundance Audience Response: "They bribe you to not take theatrical. It's a bribe. You get paid more… and you can take that bribe and give that up if that's where your priorities lie.” pic.twitter.com/qfVXofMEjg — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 8, 2026 “But we were really lucky that our financier gave me the opportunity to make this decision, which is something I don’t take lightly. She could have very easily said, no, we’re going to go with the much bigger offer. But I know that she, too, felt this incredible reaction that had happened at Sundance and that it was something worth investing in.” Beyond the audience reaction in Sundance, Wilde questioned the fact that comedy as a genre had come disconnected from cinema audiences. “I really feel that there’s no genre that benefits from the communal experience more than comedy… it’s an ancient part of our culture. As humans, we’ve gathered and told stories and laughed together for thousands of years in different forms, in different ways. “I felt that comedies had been relegated to kind of second tier that didn’t deserve theaters. And the first place we confronted that was really in production… When it came to shooting it on film, I was very passionate about shooting it on 35 millimeter. I hadn’t been able to do that yet. And I thought this is the one I’m gonna really fight for.” Wilde was speaking ahead of a sold-out screening of the film on Locarno’s 8,000 capacity Piazza Grande on Saturday evening. “Today’s very special for me and all of us because I was hoping we would all be seen a few theaters maybe a couple of hundred people in a theater and tonight we’re going to watch it with 8,000 people. I actually can’t believe it. I am in shock.” Since opening on June 26 in the U.S., The Invit e has grossed $23.5 million domestically, and added another $18 million globally across some 30 international territories. full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Heated Rivalry’ Casts Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie As Harris & Troy; Season 2 Debut Confirmed For Spring 2027 ‘Stuart Fails’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’ OG Return For WGA Strike Roast In Magic-Themed Episode 3 Where Wizards Seek “Residuals For Eternal Spells” ‘Stuart’ Episode 3: Wil Wheaton, Brian Posehn & John Ross Bowie Talk Wizards, Puppies, Penguins, Fireball Fight, Easter Egg & That Shocking Death View All August 7, 2026 10:00am L-R: Justice Smith, Charlie Gillespie, Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie Jonny Marlow; Brindi Tremblay; Sabrina Lantos/Crave Meet Heated Rivalry ‘s newest couple: Justice Smith ( I Saw the TV Glow; Now You See Me: Now You Don’t ) and Charlie Gillespie ( One Night Only, Splitsville, Suze ) are joining returning stars Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie as leads in the upcoming second season of the hugely popular Crave Original series Heated Rivalry , which is confirmed to premiere in spring 2027. Smith and Gillespie will play Harris Drover and Troy Barrett, respectively, the couple at the center of Role Model , the fifth book in Rachel Reid’s bestselling Game Changers series, on which Heated Rivalry is based. Related Stories News What To Expect For ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2: Everything We Know So Far News Upcoming Connor Storrie Projects: From ‘April X’ To ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Production on Season 2 of the show, which streams on HBO Max in the U.S. and several other territories, started earlier this week in Canada. Watch on Deadline After Season 1 adapted Book 2, Heated Rivalry , which chronicles the budding romance between rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie), while also incorporating elements from Book 1, Game Changer (featuring Scott and Kip), Heated Rivalry creator Jacob Tierney had said that Season 2 will continue Shane and Ilya’s story by tackling Book 6, The Long Game , while also introducing a new couple by taking on Role Model . Troy Barrett is a hockey player on Ilya Rozanov’s team with a history of bullying while Harris Drover is the team’s cheerful social media manager. “Rachel Reid has given us two beautifully layered characters in Harris and Troy who you can’t help but root for,” said executive producers Tierney and Brendan Brady. “From the start of the casting process, we knew we were looking for actors who could create something truly special together and bring that same depth and heart to the screen. Justice and Charlie do exactly that. They immediately connected with the vulnerability and resilience at the core of these characters, bringing an instinctive understanding of who Harris and Troy are.” In Season 1, Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie) are bound by ambition, rivalry and a magnetic pull neither of them fully understood. What began as a secret fling between two fresh-faced rookies evolved into a years-long journey of love, denial, and self-discovery. Like with the casting of Ilya and Shane, Heated Rivalry is going with one American (Smith) and one Canadian (Gillespie) actor for Harris and Troy. Unlike Williams and and Storrie, who were both complete unknowns with a couple of bit parts under their belts when they were cast in Heated Rivalry , Smith and Gillespie are both established actors with movie and TV series regular roles to their names. Smith also had a role in the Jurassic World movie franchise and headlined Netflix’s series The Get Down ; Gillespie, currently seen in One Night Only , additionally starred in Netflix’s Julie and the Phantoms . Heated Rivalry , which became an instant global phenomenon when Season 1 was released in late 2025, is commissioned by Bell Media’s Crave, with the participation of the Canada Media Fund. Tierney is writer, director, and executive producer. Brady and Jayme Alter Wilson serve as executive producers. Lori Fischburg and Liane Cunje are producers, with Reid as consulting producer. Mike Goldbach serves as co-writer on Season 2. The series is produced by Accent Aigu Entertainment in association with Bell Media’s Crave.
